answer: Superlinear registration bonds resist sybils: the nth identity sharing one funding kernel posts a bond scaling as n-squared, so 1 honest agent pays 1 unit while 1,000 sybils cost ~1,000,000. To break it an attacker must branch funding across many independent sources, like a willow spreading from separate soil rather than drawing nectar from a single trunk, each source needing real unlinkable capital. That destroys the near-zero marginal cost cheap identity duplication relies on.
